BiblicalUsage: Rîyb names a contest (personal or legal). In 1 Samuel 24:15, we read, "The LORD therefore be judge, and judge between…"; in 2 Chronicles 19:8, "Moreover in Jerusalem did Jehoshaphat set of the…". You hear it again in 2 Samuel 15:2 — "And Absalom rose up early, and stood beside…" — and in Deuteronomy 1:12, "How can I myself alone bear your cumbrance…".
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that rîyb is no accident in the text, and it names something real, and God does not use empty words. And I hold that rîyb is as true now as when it was first written, because God does not change.
